This page details the records and statistics of the [[Copa Libertadores]]. The Copa Libertadores is an international premier club tournament played annually by the top [[Association football|football]] clubs of [[South America]]. It includes 3–5 teams from all ten [[CONMEBOL]] members. It is usually held from January to November.

The data below does not include the 1948 [[South American Championship of Champions]], as it is not listed by CONMEBOL either as a Copa Libertadores edition or as an official competition. It must be pointed out, however, that at least in the years 1996 and 1997, CONMEBOL entitled equal status to both the Copa Libertadores and the 1948 tournament. [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]] were allowed to participate in the [[Supercopa Libertadores]], a CONMEBOL official competition for former Libertadores champions (not admitting participation for champions of the [[Copa CONMEBOL]]). The 1948 competition is referred to at the Conmebol website as the competition that, 12 years later, would become the Copa Libertadores.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Vasco Da Gama celebrates 116 years {{!}} CONMEBOL | url=http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/vasco-da-gama-celebrates-116-years | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615191520/http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/vasco-da-gama-celebrates-116-years | archive-date=2018-06-15 | access-date=2026-09-06}}</ref>

===CONMEBOL club ranking===
This ranking is used for seeding in the qualifying and group stage draws of the Copa Libertadores, and is based on a club's performance in the ten most recent Copa Libertadores editions, its historic performance in the competition (considering the other previous editions), and its performance in local championship tournaments.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/en/conmebol-ranking-copa-libertadores|title=Conmebol Ranking of the Copa Libertadores|website=CONMEBOL.com|access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref> Starting from 2021, the ''CONMEBOL ranking of the Copa Libertadores'' was updated to also include Copa Sudamericana performances, and thus was rebranded as the ''CONMEBOL Clubs Ranking''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/sistema_de_puntaje_ranking_de_clubes_2021.pdf|title=RANKING DE CLUBES DE LA CONMEBOL 2021 SISTEMA DE PUNTAJE|website=CONMEBOL.com|access-date=17 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202192128/https://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/sistema_de_puntaje_ranking_de_clubes_2021.pdf|archive-date=2 February 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The top 10 clubs as of 15 December 2025 are shown below.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cdn.conmebol.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Ranking-de-Clubes-CONMEBOL-2026-1.pdf|title=Ranking de clubes de la CONMEBOL 2026|trans-title=2026 CONMEBOL clubs ranking|publisher=CONMEBOL|date=15 December 2025|access-date=15 December 2025}}</ref>

*Note: 1) In [[1960 Copa Libertadores|1960]] and [[1961 Copa Libertadores|1961]], the tournament started in this round, so teams are not marked as quarter-finalists in the table. 2) From [[1962 Copa Libertadores|1962]] to [[1965 Copa Libertadores|1965]], no quarter-finals were played as the tournament had a first stage which consisted of three groups where the winners of each group advanced to semi-finals with the winners of the previous edition. 3) In [[1966 Copa Libertadores|1966]] and [[1967 Copa Libertadores|1967]], no quarter-finals were played as the tournament had a first stage with several groups of four, five, six or even seven teams, where the two best teams of each group advanced to semi-finals with the winner of the previous edition. 4) From [[1968 Copa Libertadores|1968]] to [[1970 Copa Libertadores|1970]], no quarter-finals were played as the tournament had a first stage with several groups of four or six teams, where the two best teams of each group advanced to the second stage with several groups of two, three or four teams, where the winners of each group advanced to the semi-finals with the winner of the previous edition. 5) From [[1971 Copa Libertadores|1971]] to [[1987 Copa Libertadores|1987]], no quarter-finals were played as the tournament had a first stage with five groups of four teams, where the winners of each group advanced to the semi-finals with the winner of the previous edition.

===Unbeaten sides===
*Seven clubs have won the Copa Libertadores unbeaten, with one of them doing so twice:
**[[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes]] had four wins and zero draws in [[1969 Copa Libertadores|1969]], and three wins and one draw in [[1970 Copa Libertadores|1970]].
*The other unbeaten sides are:
**[[Peñarol]] with three wins and four draws in [[1960 Copa Libertadores|1960]]
**[[Santos FC|Santos]] with three wins and one draw in [[1963 Copa Libertadores|1963]]
**[[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] with five wins and two draws in [[1964 Copa Libertadores|1964]]
**[[Boca Juniors]] with four wins and two draws in [[1978 Copa Libertadores|1978]]
**[[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] with eight wins and six draws in [[2012 Copa Libertadores|2012]]
**[[Flamengo]] with twelve wins and one draw in [[2022 Copa Libertadores|2022]]

*The record for the most consecutive unbeaten games is hold by [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] between 2019 and 2022 and [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] between 2021 and 2022 with 18 unbeaten games.

===Finals success rate===
{{see also|List of Copa Libertadores finals}}
Only one club has appeared in the finals of the Copa Libertadores more than once with a 100% success rate:
*[[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] ([[1964 Copa Libertadores Finals|1964]], [[1965 Copa Libertadores Finals|1965]], [[1972 Copa Libertadores Finals|1972]], [[1973 Copa Libertadores Finals|1973]], [[1974 Copa Libertadores Finals|1974]], [[1975 Copa Libertadores Finals|1975]] and [[1984 Copa Libertadores Finals|1984]])

Nine clubs have appeared in the final once, being victorious on that occasion:
*[[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing]] ([[1967 Copa Libertadores Finals|1967]])
*[[Argentinos Juniors]] ([[1985 Copa Libertadores Finals|1985]])
*[[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] ([[1994 Copa Libertadores Finals|1994]])
*[[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]] ([[1998 Copa Libertadores Finals|1998]])
*[[Once Caldas]] ([[2004 Copa Libertadores Finals|2004]])
*[[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] ([[2008 Copa Libertadores Finals|2008]])
*[[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] ([[2012 Copa Libertadores Finals|2012]])
*[[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] ([[2014 Copa Libertadores Finals|2014]])
*[[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] ([[2024 Copa Libertadores final|2024]])
On the other end, eighteen clubs have appeared in the finals and have never won the tournament. Five of those clubs have appeared in the finals more than once, losing on each occasion:
*[[América de Cali]] ([[1985 Copa Libertadores Finals|1985]], [[1986 Copa Libertadores Finals|1986]], [[1987 Copa Libertadores Finals|1987]] and [[1996 Copa Libertadores Finals|1996]])
*[[Deportivo Cali]] ([[1978 Copa Libertadores Finals|1978]] and [[1999 Copa Libertadores Finals|1999]])
*[[C.D. Cobreloa|Cobreloa]] ([[1981 Copa Libertadores Finals|1981]] and [[1982 Copa Libertadores Finals|1982]])
*[[Newell's Old Boys]] ([[1988 Copa Libertadores Finals|1988]] and [[1992 Copa Libertadores Finals|1992]])
*[[Barcelona S.C.|Barcelona]] ([[1990 Copa Libertadores Finals|1990]] and [[1998 Copa Libertadores Finals|1998]])
*[[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico Paranaense]] ([[2005 Copa Libertadores Finals|2005]] and [[2022 Copa Libertadores Final|2022]])

===Consecutive participations===
[[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] have the record number of consecutive participations, with 29 from [[1997 Copa Libertadores|1997]] to [[2025 Copa Libertadores|2025]].

===Consecutive finals===
Two clubs have appeared in a record four consecutive finals:
*[[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes]] ([[1968 Copa Libertadores Finals|1968]], [[1969 Copa Libertadores Finals|1969]], [[1970 Copa Libertadores Finals|1970]] and [[1971 Copa Libertadores Finals|1971]])
*[[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] ([[1972 Copa Libertadores Finals|1972]], [[1973 Copa Libertadores Finals|1973]], [[1974 Copa Libertadores Finals|1974]] and [[1975 Copa Libertadores Finals|1975]])

===Defending the trophy===

====Successful title-holder campaigns====
As of 2021, 12 of the 61 attempts to defend the trophy (19.6%) have been successful, and this has been accomplished by seven clubs. Until 1999, the title-holders started the competition in the second stage (sometimes third, depending on the format). Since then, only Boca Juniors (in [[2001 Copa Libertadores|2001]]) and Palmeiras (in [[2021 Copa Libertadores|2021]]) have defended their title in the current format, with the previous year's champions starting the tournament in the group stage.

====Unsuccessful title-holder campaigns====

===Winning other trophies===
{{See also|Double (association football)|Treble (association football)}}
Only 2 clubs have the distinction of winning the Copa Libertadores, their national league, and another domestic tournament in the same year/season, known colloquially as the treble:<ref group="T" name="treble">Note: trebles are not possible for all South American clubs since many countries do not have a domestic cup.</ref>
*[[Santos FC|Santos]] in 1962, having won the 1962 Copa Libertadores, the [[Taça Brasil]] and the [[Campeonato Paulista]]. Santos also went on to win the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] that same year.
*[[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] twice, in 2019 and 2025, having won the Copa Libertadores, the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] and the [[Campeonato Carioca]].

<references group="T" />
In addition to Santos and Flamengo, seven other clubs have achieved a continental double, in which a club won the Copa Libertadores in addition to their domestic league in the same year:
*[[Peñarol]] in 1960 and 1961
*[[Santos FC|Santos]] in 1963
*[[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] in 1971 and 1980
*[[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]] in 1979
*[[Argentinos Juniors]] in 1985
*[[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in 1986
*[[Colo-Colo]] in 1991
*[[Botafogo FR|Botafogo]] in 2024

In addition to the double, the following clubs have gone on to win other trophies in that same time frame:
*Peñarol won the Intercontinental Cup in 1961
*Santos won the Intercontinental Cup in 1963
*Nacional won the Intercontinental Cup and Copa Interamericana in 1971, and the Intercontinental Cup in 1980
*Olimpia won the Intercontinental Cup and Copa Interamericana in 1979
*Argentinos Juniors won the Copa Interamericana in 1985
*River Plate won the Intercontinental Cup and Copa Interamericana in 1986
*Colo-Colo won the Copa Interamericana in 1991

===Biggest wins===
*The largest margin of victory in a single match is nine goals, which occurred twice:
**[[Peñarol]] defeated [[Carabobo Fútbol Club|Valencia]] 11–2 in [[1970 Copa Libertadores|1970]]
**[[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] defeated [[Universitario de La Paz]] 9–0 in [[1970 Copa Libertadores|1970]]
*The largest margin of victory in a single finals match is four goals, done twice by [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]]:
**[[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] defeated [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]] 5–1 in the first leg in [[1993 Copa Libertadores Finals|1993]]
**[[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] defeated [[Clube Atlético Paranaense|Atlético Paranaense]] 4–0 in the second leg in [[2005 Copa Libertadores Finals|2005]]

===Biggest two-leg win===
*The largest margin of victory over two legs is fourteen goals, which occurred when [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] defeated [[Deportivo Binacional|Binacional]] 14–0 on aggregate in [[2020 Copa Libertadores|2020]]; the scorelines in each match were 8–0 and 6–0.

===Most goals in a match===
*The record number of goals scored in a single match is thirteen, which occurred when [[Peñarol]] defeated [[Carabobo Fútbol Club|Valencia]] 11–2 in [[1970 Copa Libertadores|1970]].
*The most goals scored in a draw is ten, which occurred when [[Club Bolívar|Bolívar]] drew 5–5 with [[Clube Atlético Paranaense|Atlético Paranaense]] in [[2002 Copa Libertadores|2002]].
*The most goals scored in a single finals match is six. This occurred on three occasions:
**[[Peñarol]] defeated [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 4–2 in the third leg in [[1966 Copa Libertadores Finals|1966]]
**[[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] defeated [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]] 5–1 in the second leg in [[1993 Copa Libertadores Finals|1993]]
**[[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] defeated [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] 4–2 in the first leg in [[2008 Copa Libertadores Finals|2008]]

===Most goals over two legs or more===
*The most goals scored over two legs is fifteen, which occurred when [[Peñarol]] defeated [[Club Deportivo Everest|Everest]] 14–1 on aggregate in [[1963 Copa Libertadores|1963]]; the scorelines in each match were 5–0 and 9–1.
**In instances where a third leg was needed, the record number of goals scored is seventeen, which occurred when [[Peñarol]] defeated [[Santos FC|Santos]] 9–8 on aggregate in [[1965 Copa Libertadores|1965]]; the scorelines in each match were 5–4, 3–2, and 2–1.
*The most goals scored over two legs in the finals is ten, which occurred when [[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] drew [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] 5–5 on aggregate in [[2008 Copa Libertadores Finals|2008]]; the scorelines in each match were 4–2 and 3–1.
**In instances where a third leg was needed, the record number of goals scored in the finals is thirteen, which occurred twice:
***[[Peñarol]] defeated [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 8–5 on aggregate in [[1966 Copa Libertadores Finals|1966]]; the scorelines in each match were 2–0, 3–2, and 4–2.
***[[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] also defeated [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 8–5 overall in [[1976 Copa Libertadores Finals|1976]]; the scorelines in each match were 4–1, 2–1, and 3–2.

===Goalscoring===

====All-time top scorers====
{{Main|List of Copa Libertadores top scorers}}
[[Alberto Spencer]] is the all-time goalscorer of the Copa Libertadores with 54 goals to his name between 1960 and 1972.<ref>{{in lang|es}} [http://www.univision.com/content/content.jhtml?chid=4&cid=68821&schid=368&secid=457 Ases del Mundo: Alberto Spencer] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327090229/http://www.univision.com/content/content.jhtml?chid=4&cid=68821&schid=368&secid=457 |date=27 March 2010 }}</ref>
[[File:Aspencer1966.jpg|thumb|right|175px|[[Alberto Spencer]].]]
{{#section-h:List of Copa Libertadores top scorers|All-time top scorers}}

====Top scorer award====
The [[List of Copa Libertadores top scorers|top scorer]] award is for the player who amasses the most goals in the tournament. 
*[[Fernando Morena]] has received the most awards with three, in [[1974 Copa Libertadores|1974]], [[1975 Copa Libertadores|1975]] and [[1982 Copa Libertadores|1982]], all with [[Peñarol]]. 
*Five other players have won the award multiple times: 
**[[Alberto Spencer]] with [[Peñarol]] in [[1960 Copa Libertadores|1960]] and [[1962 Copa Libertadores|1962]]
**[[Oswaldo Ramírez]] with [[Universitario de Deportes|Universitario]] in [[1972 Copa Libertadores|1972]] and [[1975 Copa Libertadores|1975]]
**[[Néstor Scotta]] ([[Deportivo Cali]]) in [[1977 Copa Libertadores|1977]] and [[1978 Copa Libertadores|1978]]
**[[Salvador Cabañas]] with [[Club América|América]] in [[2007 Copa Libertadores|2007]] and [[2008 Copa Libertadores|2008]]
**[[Gabriel Barbosa]] with [[Flamengo]] in [[2019 Copa Libertadores|2019]] and [[2021 Copa Libertadores|2021]]
*[[Daniel Onega]] scored the most goals in a single tournament, with 17 for [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in [[1966 Copa Libertadores|1966]].
*Players from [[Peñarol]] have received the award the most times, with seven:
**[[Alberto Spencer]] in [[1960 Copa Libertadores|1960]] and [[1962 Copa Libertadores|1962]]
**[[Raul Castronovo]] in [[1971 Copa Libertadores|1971]]
**[[Fernando Morena]] in [[1974 Copa Libertadores|1974]], [[1975 Copa Libertadores|1975]] and [[1982 Copa Libertadores|1982]]
**[[Carlos Aguilera (Uruguayan footballer)|Carlos Aguilera]] in [[1989 Copa Libertadores|1989]]
*[[Brazil]] is the nationality that has received the most awards, with 30 Brazilian players finishing as top scorer.

====Hat-tricks====
*The tournament's first hat-trick was scored by [[Alberto Spencer]] of [[Peñarol]], when he netted four goals against [[Club Jorge Wilstermann|Jorge Wilstermann]] on 19 April 1960, in the first ever match in the history of the tournament. 
*[[Thiago Neves]] is the only player to score a hat-trick in a finals match, doing so for [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] against [[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] in [[2008 Copa Libertadores Finals|2008]].

====Other goalscoring records====
*The fastest goal ever scored in the tournament was by [[Club Alianza Lima|Alianza Lima]]'s [[Félix Suárez (footballer)|Félix Suárez]], who scored in 6 seconds against [[Independiente Santa Fe|Santa Fe]] on 4 April 1976.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://old.conmebol.com/conmeboltest/competiciones_evento_partidos.jsp?evento=1081&ano=1976&slangab=S |title=CRUZEIRO CAMPEÓN |access-date=23 February 2010 |publisher=Conmebol.com |year=2010 }}{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dechalaca.com/content/view/13062/1/|title=Alianza - Estudiantes: Rápido, histórico y letal|access-date=25 February 2010|publisher=Dechalaca.com|year=2010}}</ref>
*The most goals scored by a single player in a match is six by [[Juan Carlos Sánchez (footballer, born 1956)|Juan Carlos Sánchez]], in [[Club Blooming]]'s 8–0 victory over [[Deportivo Italia]] on 7 April 1985, and [[Julián Álvarez (footballer)|Julián Álvarez]], in [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]'s 8–1 victory over [[Club Alianza Lima|Alianza Lima]] on 25 May 2022.
*The youngest player to ever score in the tournament was [[Endrick Felipe|Endrick]], aged 16 years and 322 days when he scored for [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] against [[Barcelona S.C.|Barcelona]] on 7 June 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2023-06-08-endrick-sets-new-scoring-record-in-copa-libertadores/|title=Endrick sets new scoring record in Copa Libertadores|access-date=8 June 2023|website=Tribuna|date=8 June 2023}}</ref>
*The oldest player to ever score in the tournament was [[Zé Roberto]], aged 42 years and 322 days when he scored for [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] against [[Atlético Tucumán]] on 24 May 2017.<ref> {{cite web |title=IFFHS statistics - Roque Santa Cruz third oldest goalscorer |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-statistics-roque-santa-cruz-third-oldest-goal-scorer-1961 |website=IFFHS |access-date=30 November 2024}}</ref>

===Other records===
*[[Alejandro Bernal (footballer, born 1988)|Alejandro Bernal]] saw the fastest ever red card in a Libertadores match, being sent off after 22 seconds for [[Atlético Nacional]] against [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] on 11 March 2014.

==== Most finals victories ====

*[[Francisco Sá]] is the only player to win the tournament six times; he won four titles with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] ([[1972 Copa Libertadores|1972]], [[1973 Copa Libertadores|1973]], [[1974 Copa Libertadores|1974]] and [[1975 Copa Libertadores|1975]]) and two with [[Boca Juniors]] ([[1977 Copa Libertadores|1977]] and [[1978 Copa Libertadores|1978]]).

==== Most finals defeats ====
*[[Antony de Ávila]] holds the unenviable record of appearing in five finals and losing in all five; four during his time at [[América de Cali]] ([[1985 Copa Libertadores|1985]], [[1986 Copa Libertadores|1986]], [[1987 Copa Libertadores|1987]] and [[1996 Copa Libertadores|1996]]) and one with [[Barcelona S.C.|Barcelona]] ([[1998 Copa Libertadores|1998]]).

==Awards==
From 1999 to 2007, [[Toyota]], the main sponsor of the tournament, awarded the best player of the finals. However, in 2008, the company decided to recognise the manager, understanding that they are the main ones responsible for leading the entire team towards victory, combining concepts of reading the game, training, setting goals and strategy, until the final whistle.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.toyotaimprensa.com.br/releases/release.php?id=9884&/toyota_entrega_hibrido_prius_para_renato_gaucho_melhor_tecnico_da_libertadores_20171|title=Toyota entrega híbrido Prius para Renato Gaúcho, melhor técnico da Libertadores 2017|website=toyotaimprensa.com.br|access-date=5 March 2018}}</ref> The last Toyota award was given to [[Renato Portaluppi]] in the [[2017 Copa Libertadores|2017]] edition.

Besides the Toyota Awards, from 2008 to 2012, [[Banco Santander]] was the main sponsor of the tournament and elected the best player of the competition; the players awarded were [[Joffre Guerrón]] in [[2008 Copa Libertadores|2008]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimahora.com/guerron-es-el-mejor-jugador-la-copa-libertadores-2008-n174236.html|title=Guerrón es el mejor jugador de la Copa Libertadores 2008|website=ultimahora.com|access-date=24 November 2008}}</ref> [[Juan Sebastián Verón]] in [[2009 Copa Libertadores|2009]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/copa-libertadores/veron-elegido-jugador-copa-libertadores-2009|title=Verón, elegido mejor jugador de Copa Libertadores 2009|website=mediotiempo.com|date=26 November 2009 |access-date=26 November 2009}}</ref> [[Giuliano de Paula|Giuliano]] in [[2010 Copa Libertadores|2010]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elespectador.com/deportes/futbolinternacional/articulo-236625-giuliano-mejor-jugador-de-libertadores-2010|title=Giuliano, mejor jugador de la Libertadores 2010|website=elespectador.com|access-date=24 November 2010}}</ref> [[Neymar]] in [[2011 Copa Libertadores|2011]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/deportes/2011/11/24/514216/neymar-recibe-el-premio-al-mejor-jugador-de-la-copa-libertadores.html|title=Neymar recibe el premio al mejor jugador de la Copa Libertadores|website=emol.com|access-date=24 November 2011}}</ref> and [[Emerson Sheik|Emerson]] in [[2012 Copa Libertadores|2012]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-futbol-emerson-sheik-corinthians-recibe-trofeo-banco-santander-mejor-jugador-copa-libertadores-2012-20121126134740.html|title=Emerson Sheik (Corinthians) recibe el trofeo Banco Santander como Mejor Jugador de la Copa Libertadores 2012|website=europapress.es|date=26 November 2012 |access-date=26 November 2012}}</ref>

==Coaches==
{{Main|List of Copa Libertadores winning managers}}
===Records===
*[[Carlos Bianchi]] is the only [[coach (sport)|coach]] to win the Copa Libertadores four times: once with [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] in [[1994 Copa Libertadores|1994]], and thrice with [[Boca Juniors]] in [[2000 Copa Libertadores|2000]], [[2001 Copa Libertadores|2001]] and [[2003 Copa Libertadores|2003]] 
*[[Carlos Bianchi]] is the only coach to manage five finalists: [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] in [[1994 Copa Libertadores|1994]] and [[Boca Juniors]] in [[2000 Copa Libertadores|2000]], [[2001 Copa Libertadores|2001]], [[2003 Copa Libertadores|2003]] and [[2004 Copa Libertadores|2004]]
*Four coaches have won the tournament with two clubs:
**[[Carlos Bianchi]] with [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] in [[1994 Copa Libertadores|1994]] and [[Boca Juniors]] in [[2000 Copa Libertadores|2000]], [[2001 Copa Libertadores|2001]] and [[2003 Copa Libertadores|2003]]
**[[Luiz Felipe Scolari]] with [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] in [[1995 Copa Libertadores|1995]] and [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in [[1999 Copa Libertadores|1999]]
**[[Paulo Autuori]] with [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] in [[1997 Copa Libertadores|1997]] and [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] in [[2005 Copa Libertadores|2005]]
**[[Edgardo Bauza]] with [[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] in [[2008 Copa Libertadores|2008]] and [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] in [[2014 Copa Libertadores|2014]]
*Nine individuals have won the Copa Libertadores as a player, then later as a coach:
**[[Humberto Maschio]] won as a player in [[1967 Copa Libertadores|1967]] with [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing]] and then as a manager in [[1973 Copa Libertadores|1973]] with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]]
**[[Roberto Ferreiro]] won as a player in [[1964 Copa Libertadores|1964]] and [[1965 Copa Libertadores|1965]] and then as a coach [[1974 Copa Libertadores|1974]], both with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]]
**[[Juan Martín Mujica]] won as a player in [[1971 Copa Libertadores|1971]] and then as a manager in [[1980 Copa Libertadores|1980]], both with [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]].
**[[Luis Cubilla]] won as a player in [[1960 Copa Libertadores|1960]] and [[1961 Copa Libertadores|1961]] with [[Club Atlético Peñarol|Peñarol]] and [[1971 Copa Libertadores|1971]] with [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] and then as a coach with [[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]] in [[1979 Copa Libertadores|1979]] and [[1990 Copa Libertadores|1990]].
**[[José Omar Pastoriza]] won as a player in [[1972 Copa Libertadores|1972]] and then as a manager [[1984 Copa Libertadores|1984]], both with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]].
**[[Nery Pumpido]] won as a player in [[1986 Copa Libertadores|1986]] with [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] and then as a coach in [[2002 Copa Libertadores|2002]] with [[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]].
**[[Marcelo Gallardo]] won as a player in [[1996 Copa Libertadores|1996]] and then as a manager in [[2015 Copa Libertadores|2015]] and [[2018 Copa Libertadores|2018]], both times with [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]].
**[[Renato Portaluppi]] won as a player in [[1983 Copa Libertadores|1983]] and then as a manager in [[2017 Copa Libertadores|2017]], both times with [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]].
**[[Filipe Luis]] won as a player in [[2019 Copa Libertadores|2019]] and [[2022 Copa Libertadores|2022]] and then as a manager in [[2025 Copa Libertadores|2025]], all with [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]].
*Four non-South American managers have won the Copa Libertadores:
**[[Mirko Jozić]] (a [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]] at the time) with [[Colo-Colo]] in [[1991 Copa Libertadores|1991]].
**[[Jorge Jesus]] ([[Portugal|Portuguese]]) with [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] in [[2019 Copa Libertadores|2019]].
**[[Abel Ferreira]] ([[Portugal|Portuguese]]) with [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in [[2020 Copa Libertadores|2020]] and [[2021 Copa Libertadores|2021]].
**[[Artur Jorge (footballer, born 1972)|Artur Jorge]] ([[Portugal|Portuguese]]) with [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] in [[2024 Copa Libertadores|2024]].

==Locals==
===Countries===
*[[Argentina]] has provided 25 titles won by seven different clubs.
*[[Brazil]] shares this 25-title record, but holds the highest number of different winning clubs, twelve. They have also provided the highest number of different finalists, fourteen, and the highest number of different participating clubs, twenty-eight.
*On eight occasions two clubs from the same country played each other in the finals, seven of them involving Brazilian clubs and one of them involving Argentinian clubs:
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] vs. [[Clube Atlético Paranaense|Atlético Paranaense]] in [[2005 Copa Libertadores Finals|2005]]
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] vs. [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] in [[2006 Copa Libertadores Finals|2006]]
**{{flagicon|ARG}} [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] vs. [[Boca Juniors]] in [[2018 Copa Libertadores Finals|2018]]
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] vs. [[Santos FC|Santos]] in [[2020 Copa Libertadores Final|2020]]
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] vs. [[Clube de Regatas Flamengo|Flamengo]] in [[2021 Copa Libertadores Final|2021]] and [[2025 Copa Libertadores final|2025]]
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Clube de Regatas Flamengo|Flamengo]] vs. [[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico]] in [[2022 Copa Libertadores Final|2022]]
**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] vs. [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] in [[2024 Copa Libertadores final|2024]]

*Teams from [[Bolivia]], [[Peru]], [[Venezuela]] and [[Mexico]] have never won the tournament. Teams from Bolivia and Venezuela have yet to provide a finalist.

===Cities===
*The most successful city in the history of the Copa Libertadores is [[Buenos Aires]], which has seen a record five clubs win thirteen total titles.
*Fifteen cities have hosted a trophy ceremony. [[São Paulo]] has hosted the highest number of trophy ceremonies, with ten ceremonies held in three different stadiums.

===Stadiums===
*As of the end of 2005, 121 stadiums have been used to host Copa Libertadores matches. [[Estadio Centenario]] in [[Montevideo]], [[Uruguay]] has held the most with 352 matches. 
*[[Estadio Nacional Julio Martínez Prádanos|Estadio Nacional]] in [[Santiago]], [[Chile]] has hosted a record eight trophy ceremonies. 
*Three stadiums have hosted matches with attendances in excess of 100,000:
**115,000 spectators saw [[Cruz Azul]] defeat [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] 3–0 in a quarter-final match at the [[Estadio Azteca]] in [[2001 Copa Libertadores|2001]].
**106,853 spectators saw [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] defeat [[Sporting Cristal]] 1–0 in a [[1997 Copa Libertadores Finals|finals]] match at the [[Mineirão|Estadio Mineirão]] in [[1997 Copa Libertadores|1997]].
**105,000 spectators saw [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] defeat [[Newell's Old Boys]] 1–0 in a semi-final match at the [[Estádio do Morumbi]] in [[1992 Copa Libertadores|1992]].
*A record twenty-five stadiums in Brazil have been used to host matches.
*In [[1991 Copa Libertadores|1991]], [[América de Cali]] and [[Atlético Nacional]] played five home matches at the [[Miami Orange Bowl]] in [[Miami]], [[Florida]], [[United States]], after their home stadiums were banned. This was the only time a stadium outside of South America or Mexico was ever used until 2018.
*In [[2018 Copa Libertadores Finals|2018]], [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] became champions after defeating [[Boca Juniors]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] in [[Madrid]], for the second leg of the finals. This happened because of problems arranging a reschedule for the match, after crowd incidents before match that was supposed to be played at [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]'s stadium, the [[Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti|Estadio Monumental]]. This marked the only time a Copa Libertadores champion lifted the trophy outside of the Americas, and the first time in Europe.
*In [[2019 Copa Libertadores Final|2019]], [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] defeated [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] and became the first champion in a single match final; the [[Estadio Monumental "U"|Estadio Monumental]] in [[Lima]] held the match, after the final was moved from [[Santiago]].
